project.projectDesc: Adds Google Drive file operations to a provider-neutral cloud-storage interface developed as graduate open-source work.

caseStudy.summary: This graduate open-source contribution adds Google Drive file operations to the CloudMesh multi-cloud storage interface. I implemented provider integration so users can perform common storage actions through a shared abstraction instead of calling provider-specific operations directly.
caseStudy.challenge: Cloud providers expose different APIs, authentication models, and file metadata. A common storage interface must normalize those differences while still supporting useful provider operations.
caseStudy.architecture: CloudMesh presents a unified storage interface and delegates file operations to a provider adapter. The Google Drive adapter translates those operations into Google Drive API requests and returns normalized results.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart LR
  User[CloudMesh user] --> API[Unified storage interface]
  API --> Adapter[Google Drive adapter]
  Adapter --> Auth[Provider authentication]
  Auth --> Drive[Google Drive API]
  Drive --> Adapter
  Adapter --> API
  API --> User
contributions: Implemented Google Drive integration within the CloudMesh storage abstraction.
Added file operations to store, access, retrieve, list, update, and delete files.
Contributed a Python SDK surface for working with Google Drive through CloudMesh.
tradeoffs: A provider-neutral interface simplifies common workflows, while provider-specific capabilities and limits still need explicit handling.
The abstraction improves portability but adds an adapter layer that must preserve authentication and operation semantics.
Provider adapters preserve each service's authentication and file semantics behind the shared interface.

scale: The broader project supports providers such as Google Cloud, Google Drive, AWS, and Azure.
business: The unified interface reduces the need to learn provider-specific file operations.
quality: The contribution covers common create, read, update, delete, and listing operations.
